nodes.label: The full reference.conf
nodes.rationale: The framework's built-in configuration reproduced exactly as it ships in src/config/reference.ts - the complete set of first-party settings. Anything not in it has no HOCON form, and every value shown is the default already in effect, so only overrides belong in application.conf.

nodes.label: No dead keys
nodes.rationale: For a long stretch about twenty-five documented settings were never read - you could set sharding.passivation-idle, get no passivation and no warning (#653). A test now walks every leaf and asserts it is both reachable from ConfigKeys and referenced from source, so a dead key is a build failure. The exemption list still exists and every entry must name the issue that removes it; it is currently empty.

nodes.label: logger.sinks blocks
nodes.rationale: Every sink ships disabled; enabling at least one replaces the default single ConsoleLogger with a MultiSinkLogger. An explicit logger passed to ActorSystem.create replaces the whole block rather than merging - a sink belongs to one construction world or the other. Credentials and TLS key material are deliberately code-only.

nodes.label: dead-letters settings
nodes.rationale: Undeliverable messages are published on the event stream either way; this block decides whether anything KEEPS them. The queue is a diagnostic ring because an unbounded one turns a delivery outage into an out-of-memory, and max-replays stops a poison message being retried forever.

nodes.label: cluster.bootstrap stable-observation block
nodes.rationale: Poll discovery until the contact-point set has been unchanged for stable-margin, then let only the lowest-addressed node form a cluster if no peer promoted it within self-election-grace. Opt-in. required-contact-points is the knob worth changing: 1 keeps single-node development working, but only a value matching the expected replica count catches discovery that is stably wrong rather than merely slow.

nodes.label: coordinated-shutdown.auto-register-tasks
nodes.rationale: Framework components register their own teardown in the pipeline (HTTP unbind, broker close, cluster leave, DevTools detach); set false when an embedder owns the lifecycle of the resources it handed the system.

nodes.label: What is deliberately not in reference.conf
nodes.rationale: Plugin subtrees (journals, snapshot stores, caches, brokers) are optional peers, so shipping defaults for them would mean shipping configuration for a package you may not have installed. And anything that is not a value - entity actors, extractors, allocation strategies, leases, transports, downing providers - cannot be expressed by a config file and stays in code behind an XOptions builder.

nodes.label: Precedence is per field, not per block
nodes.rationale: Setting one failure-detector threshold in code leaves the other two coming from your config file; an undefined in code means 'not set' and falls through rather than blanking the layer below.

nodes.label: system.shutdown-drain-timeout
nodes.rationale: How long terminate() lets /user actors finish queued work before the stop cascade. The wait ends as soon as the tree goes quiet, so an idle system pays a tick; keep it under coordinated-shutdown.default-phase-timeout because the last phase awaits terminate(). A throttled or suspended mailbox is never waited on.
